questions.question: Which of the following is a polynomial in x?
questions.explanation: A polynomial has only non-negative integer powers of x. Only 3x<sup>2</sup> − 4x + 7 satisfies this.

questions.question: What is the degree of the polynomial P(x) = 4x<sup>5</sup> − 3x<sup>3</sup> + 7x − 9?
questions.explanation: The degree is the highest power of x, which is 5.

questions.question: If P(x) = 2x<sup>3</sup> − kx<sup>2</sup> + 4x − 1 and the coefficient of x<sup>2</sup> is −6, find k.
questions.explanation: The coefficient of x<sup>2</sup> is −k. So −k = −6 ⇒ k = 6.

questions.question: Find the remainder when the polynomial P(x) = x<sup>3</sup> − 4x<sup>2</sup> + 5x − 2 is divided by (x − 1).
questions.explanation: By the remainder theorem, remainder = P(1) = 1 − 4 + 5 − 2 = 0.

questions.question: If (x − 2) is a factor of the polynomial P(x) = x<sup>3</sup> + ax<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 8, find the value of a.
Factorize completely: x<sup>2</sup> − 9
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares: x<sup>2</sup> − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3).

questions.question: Factorize: 2x<sup>2</sup> − 7x + 3
questions.explanation: 2x<sup>2</sup> − 7x + 3 = 2x<sup>2</sup> − 6x − x + 3 = 2x(x − 3) − 1(x − 3) = (2x − 1)(x − 3). Option 4 is equivalent.

questions.question: If P(x) = x<sup>3</sup> − 6x<sup>2</sup> + 11x − 6, which of the following is a factor of P(x)?
How many zeros does the polynomial P(x) = 5x<sup>4</sup> − 2x<sup>2</sup> + 1 have?
questions.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, a degree 4 polynomial has 4 zeros counting complex and multiplicity. It has no real zeros.

questions.question: Given that α and β are roots of the equation x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 6 = 0, find the value of αβ.
questions.explanation: For ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0, product of roots = c/a = 6/1 = 6.

questions.question: Which of the following expressions is NOT a polynomial?
questions.explanation: 3x<sup>−2</sup> + 2 has a negative exponent, so it is not a polynomial.

questions.question: The degree of the polynomial 5 − 3x<sup>2</sup> + 7x<sup>6</sup> − x<sup>4</sup> is:
questions.explanation: The highest power is 6.

questions.question: If P(x) = ax<sup>3</sup> − 4x<sup>2</sup> + bx − 7 is a polynomial of degree 3, which condition must hold?
questions.explanation: For degree 3, the coefficient of x<sup>3</sup> must be non-zero: a ≠ 0.

questions.question: Find the remainder when P(x) = 3x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 4 is divided by (x + 2).
If (x − 1) is a factor of x<sup>3</sup> + px<sup>2</sup> − x − 3, find p.
Factorize completely: x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> − 6x
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> − 6x = x(x<sup>2</sup> − x − 6) = x(x − 3)(x + 2).

questions.question: Which of the following is a quadratic polynomial?
questions.explanation: A quadratic polynomial has degree 2. Only x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 1 qualifies.

questions.question: If P(x) = x<sup>3</sup> − 4x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 12, which of the following is a factor?
The sum of the coefficients of the polynomial 2x<sup>3</sup> − 5x<sup>2</sup> + 4x − 1 is:
questions.explanation: Sum of coefficients = P(1) = 2 − 5 + 4 − 1 = 0.

questions.question: Which of the following is a zero of the polynomial x<sup>2</sup> − 9?
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − 9 = 0 ⇒ x = ±3. So 3 is a zero.

questions.question: Factorize by grouping: x<sup>3</sup> + 2x<sup>2</sup> − x − 2
questions.explanation: Group: x<sup>2</sup>(x + 2) − 1(x + 2) = (x + 2)(x<sup>2</sup> − 1).

questions.question: Factorize: x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6
How many terms are in the polynomial 7x<sup>3</sup> − 2x + 9?
questions.explanation: The terms are 7x<sup>3</sup>, −2x, and 9: three terms.

questions.question: If (x − 4) is a factor of 2x<sup>3</sup> − kx<sup>2</sup> − 8x + 16, find k.
questions.explanation: P(4) = 0 ⇒ 2(64) − k(16) − 32 + 16 = 0 ⇒ 128 − 16k − 16 = 0 ⇒ 112 = 16k ⇒ k = 7. This is not among the listed options.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE?
options: A constant is not a polynomial
A polynomial can have negative powers
A polynomial may have fractional powers
A constant is a polynomial of degree zero
questions.explanation: A non-zero constant is a polynomial of degree 0.

questions.question: Factorize completely: 4x<sup>2</sup> − 25
questions.explanation: Difference of squares: 4x<sup>2</sup> − 25 = (2x)<sup>2</sup> − 5<sup>2</sup> = (2x − 5)(2x + 5).

questions.question: If P(x) = x<sup>3</sup> + ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + 6 and −2 is a root, which equation is correct?
The highest power of the variable in a polynomial is called the:
questions.explanation: The highest power is called the degree.

questions.question: Which polynomial has exactly three zeros?
questions.explanation: A degree 3 polynomial has exactly three zeros counting complex and multiplicity. 2x<sup>3</sup> − 5x<sup>2</sup> + 1 is degree 3.

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 10 = 0, find α + β.
questions.explanation: Sum of roots = −b/a = −7/1 = −7.

questions.question: Factorize completely: x<sup>3</sup> − 8
questions.explanation: Difference of cubes: a<sup>3</sup> − b<sup>3</sup> = (a − b)(a<sup>2</sup> + ab + b<sup>2</sup>). Here x<sup>3</sup> − 8 = (x − 2)(x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 4).

questions.question: Find the remainder when x<sup>3</sup> − 3x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 7 is divided by x − 1
If x<sup>2</sup> − 3x + 2 = 0, find the product of the roots
questions.explanation: Product of roots = c/a = 2/1 = 2.

questions.question: Which of the following is a factor of x<sup>3</sup> + 2x<sup>2</sup> − x − 2?
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> + 2x<sup>2</sup> − x − 2 = (x + 2)(x − 1)(x + 1). So x + 2 is a factor (also x − 1 and x + 1).

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>4</sup> − 16 completely
Find k if (x − 2)<sup>2</sup> is a factor of x<sup>3</sup> − 6x<sup>2</sup> + kx + 12
questions.explanation: For (x − 2)<sup>2</sup> to be a factor, both P(2) = 0 and P'(2) = 0. P(2) = 8 − 24 + 2k + 12 = 2k − 4 ⇒ k = 2. P'(x) = 3x<sup>2</sup> − 12x + k ⇒ P'(2) = 12 − 24 + k = k − 12 ⇒ k = 12. Contradiction, so no such k exists.

questions.question: How many real roots does x<sup>3</sup> − 3x + 1 = 0 have?
questions.explanation: The cubic has three real roots. f(−2) < 0, f(−1) > 0, f(1) < 0, f(2) > 0, so roots lie in (−2,−1), (0,1), and (1,2).

questions.question: Find k if x<sup>2</sup> + kx + 9 has equal roots
questions.explanation: Equal roots ⇒ discriminant = 0 ⇒ k<sup>2</sup> − 4(1)(9) = 0 ⇒ k<sup>2</sup> = 36 ⇒ k = ±6. Positive option is 6.

questions.question: Which of the following divides x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup> exactly?
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup> = (x − y)(x + y), so x − y divides it exactly.

questions.question: If a polynomial has sum of coefficients zero, which of the following is a factor?
questions.explanation: Sum of coefficients = P(1). If P(1) = 0, then (x − 1) is a factor.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup> − 8 completely
questions.explanation: Difference of cubes: x<sup>3</sup> − 8 = (x − 2)(x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 4).

questions.question: Find a factor of x<sup>4</sup> − 1 given that f(1) = 0 and f(−1) = 0
questions.explanation: x<sup>4</sup> − 1 = (x<sup>2</sup> − 1)(x<sup>2</sup> + 1) = (x − 1)(x + 1)(x<sup>2</sup> + 1). Thus x<sup>2</sup> − 1 is a factor.

questions.question: Expand (x − 1)<sup>2</sup>(x + 2) and find coefficient of x<sup>2</sup>
questions.explanation: (x − 1)<sup>2</sup>(x + 2) = (x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 1)(x + 2) = x<sup>3</sup> + 2x<sup>2</sup> − 2x<sup>2</sup> − 4x + x + 2 = x<sup>3</sup> − 3x + 2. Coefficient of x<sup>2</sup> is 0.

questions.question: If the roots of x<sup>3</sup> − 6x<sup>2</sup> + 11x − 6 = 0 are α, β, γ, find α + β + γ
questions.explanation: Sum of roots = −(coefficient of x<sup>2</sup>)/(coefficient of x<sup>3</sup>) = −(−6)/1 = 6.

questions.question: Which of the following polynomials has no real roots?
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> + 4 = 0 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> = −4, which has no real solution.

questions.question: Find p if 1 is a root of x<sup>3</sup> − px<sup>2</sup> + 9x − 3
questions.explanation: P(1) = 0 ⇒ 1 − p + 9 − 3 = 0 ⇒ 7 − p = 0 ⇒ p = 7. This is not among the listed options.

questions.question: Factorize completely: 2x<sup>3</sup> + 5x<sup>2</sup> − 3x
If 2x<sup>2</sup> − 3x + 1 = 0, find product of roots
questions.explanation: Product of roots = c/a = 1/2.

questions.question: If x = 3 is a root of 27x<sup>3</sup> − 81x<sup>2</sup> + 18x + 9a = 0, find a
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 3: 27(27) − 81(9) + 18(3) + 9a = 729 − 729 + 54 + 9a = 54 + 9a = 0 ⇒ a = −6. This is not among the listed options.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of zeros a polynomial of degree 5 can have?
questions.explanation: A polynomial of degree n has at most n zeros. So degree 5 has at most 5 zeros.
